name: fastlight
description: A Spotlight-style launcher for macOS that finds any app or file in microseconds.

paragraphs: A Spotlight-style launcher for macOS that finds any app or file in about a millisecond.
Features • Install • Usage • Replace Spotlight • Extensions • Build from source • How it works • Website

Press ⌥Space anywhere, type a few letters, hit ↵. Fastlight searches your applications and your whole disk as you type, with fuzzy matching that forgives typos, and stays out of the way in the menu bar. File search is done by fsearch, which is bundled inside the app: there is nothing else to install.
features: Apps and files, kept apart. A Top Hit, then Applications with their real icons, then Files, each in its own section.
Fast, all the time. Name search over millions of files in about a millisecond, so results update on every keystroke with no debounce.
Forgiving matching. vsc finds Visual Studio Code, sys set finds System Settings, mian.rs still finds main.rs. Apps you open often move up.

Search inside files. grep:, regex: and sym: search file contents through fsearch's index and show the matching line. ↵ opens it at that line in VS Code, Cursor, VSCodium, Zed, BBEdit or TextMate, when one of them is the…
Power-user filters. ext:, in:, size:, mtime:, kind: and more, straight from the search field.

requirements.text: No network access, no accounts, no telemetry. (Extensions you install can do whatever their code does.)

The exception is fsearch's own login agent (fsearch install --login): launchd would restart it straight away, so Fastlight uses it as is, and Full Disk Access has to be granted to /.local/bin/fsearch instead.
